workedExamples.title: Solving an AND ("between") inequality as a three-part chain: −1 ≤ 2x + 3 < 9

steps.prompt: The expression 2x + 3 is trapped between two bounds at once: it must be at least −1 AND less than 9. How do we keep both conditions true while we solve?
steps.reveal: Treat it as one connected chain: −1 ≤ 2x + 3 < 9. Whatever we do to the middle, we must do to BOTH the left and right ends at the same time. The two conditions stay linked the whole way.

steps.prompt: Subtract 3 from all three parts to start isolating x.
steps.reveal: −1 − 3 ≤ 2x + 3 − 3 < 9 − 3 gives −4 ≤ 2x < 6. The middle now has just 2x left.

steps.prompt: Divide all three parts by 2. (Note: 2 is positive, so no inequality signs flip.)
Graph the solution and describe it. Which endpoints are open and which are closed?
steps.reveal: On a number line, draw a CLOSED dot at −2 (because of ≤, x can equal −2) and an OPEN dot at 3 (because of <, x cannot equal 3), then shade the segment BETWEEN them. The solution is every number from −2 up to but not including 3: −2 ≤ x < 3.

steps.prompt: Why is the answer a single bounded segment and not two separate rays?
steps.reveal: Because AND means BOTH conditions must hold together, the solution is the OVERLAP (intersection) of x ≥ −2 and x < 3 — the stretch where the two shadings cover the same ground. That overlap is one connected piece between the bounds.

workedExamples.title: Solving an OR (union) inequality and seeing why it is NOT an intersection: 2x − 1 < −7 OR x + 2 ≥ 6

steps.prompt: This is an OR statement: x only has to satisfy ONE side to be a solution. Solve each inequality separately. Start with 2x − 1 < −7.
steps.reveal: Add 1 to both sides: 2x < −6. Divide by 2: x < −3.

steps.prompt: Now solve the other side: x + 2 ≥ 6.
Graph both pieces on one number line. What does the picture look like?
steps.reveal: An OPEN dot at −3 shading LEFT (x < −3), and a CLOSED dot at 4 shading RIGHT (x ≥ 4). Two separate rays pointing in opposite directions, with a gap between −3 and 4.

steps.prompt: A classmate writes the answer as −3 < x ≤ 4 (the gap in the middle). Why is that wrong?
steps.reveal: That classmate found the INTERSECTION — the numbers in the gap belong to NEITHER inequality, so they are exactly the WRONG ones. OR asks for numbers in EITHER ray. The middle gap is empty of solutions, not full of them.

x < −3 OR x ≥ 4 — the UNION of the two rays. There is no single chain that captures it because the two pieces point in opposite directions and never connect. That is why an OR answer is described as a union, never squeezed into one between-statement.

p1.prompt: An umpire's strike zone for a batter spans heights from 18 inches up to 42 inches — a pitch counts as a strike when its height h is at least 18 AND at most 42. Type the compound inequality for a strike, in the form 18 <= h <= 42.
hints: "At least 18" means h ≥ 18; "at most 42" means h ≤ 42. Both must hold, so write them as one chain.
Type it as 18 <= h <= 42.

p1.prompt: A scout only logs a pitch when its speed s is between 88 and 96 mph — strictly faster than 88 AND strictly slower than 96. Type the compound inequality, in the form 88 < s < 96.
hints: "Strictly faster than 88" is s > 88; "strictly slower than 96" is s < 96. Both bounds must appear.
Type both bounds as one chain: 88 < s < 96.

p1.prompt: A reliever is pulled if he gives up 4 or more runs OR throws 30 or more pitches in an inning. Let r be runs allowed and p be pitches thrown. Which describes when he is pulled?
hints: He is pulled if EITHER thing happens — only one needs to be true.
"Either ... or ..." is an OR, not an AND that requires both.

p1.prompt: A pitch-tracking alert fires for any pitch thrown below 70 mph OR above 100 mph (the system flags off-speed trick pitches and elite fastballs, ignoring everything in between). Let v be the pitch speed. Which describes the flagged pitches?
hints: Flagged pitches are the EXTREMES — slow ones or fast ones — not the ones in the middle.
No single number can be both below 70 and above 100, so "and" is impossible here; it must be OR, giving two separate rays.

p1.prompt: A drill is legal only when the pitch speed s is at least 55 mph AND at most 65 mph. Type the compound inequality for a legal speed, in the form 55 <= s <= 65.
hints: "At least 55" is s ≥ 55; "at most 65" is s ≤ 65. Both must hold.
Type it as 55 <= s <= 65.

p1.prompt: A bat is tournament-legal only when its length L is more than 26 inches AND less than 34 inches. Type the compound inequality, in the form 26 < L < 34.
hints: "More than 26" is L > 26; "less than 34" is L < 34. Capture both bounds.
Type both bounds as one chain: 26 < L < 34.

p1.prompt: A runner is automatically out if she leaves the base early OR misses the bag entirely. Let either rules violation trigger the out. Using conditions A and B, which describes when she is out?
hints: Either violation alone is enough to call her out.
"Either ... or ..." is an OR; she does not need to do both.

p1.prompt: A pitching machine is sent for service whenever its release speed s drops below 40 mph OR climbs above 70 mph (too weak or too dangerous). Speeds in between are fine. Which describes the speeds that trigger service?
hints: Service is triggered at the EXTREMES — too slow or too fast — not the safe middle range.
A speed can't be both below 40 and above 70 at once, so it must be OR: two separate rays.

p1.prompt: A player's minutes m for a game are planned to be at least 24 AND at most 32. Type the compound inequality for the planned minutes, in the form 24 <= m <= 32.
hints: "At least 24" is m ≥ 24; "at most 32" is m ≤ 32. Both must hold.
Type it as 24 <= m <= 32.

p1.prompt: A scoring run is logged only when a team scores more than 6 AND fewer than 14 unanswered points. Let p be the unanswered points. Type the compound inequality, in the form 6 < p < 14.
hints: "More than 6" is p > 6; "fewer than 14" is p < 14. Capture both bounds.
Type both bounds as one chain: 6 < p < 14.

p1.prompt: A coach benches a player to avoid foul trouble if the player has 4 or more fouls OR has played 36 or more minutes. Let f be fouls and m be minutes. Which describes when the player is benched?
hints: Either reason alone is enough to bench the player.
"Either ... or ..." is an OR; both do not have to be true.

p1.prompt: A shot chart highlights only extreme attempts: shots taken closer than 3 feet (rim attacks) OR farther than 24 feet (deep threes), ignoring mid-range. Let d be the shot distance in feet. Which describes the highlighted shots?
hints: Highlighted shots are the EXTREMES — very close or very far — not the mid-range in between.
A shot can't be both under 3 ft and over 24 ft, so it must be OR: two separate rays.

p1.prompt: A youth squad is open only to players whose age a is at least 13 AND at most 14. Type the compound inequality for an eligible age, in the form 13 <= a <= 14.
hints: "At least 13" is a ≥ 13; "at most 14" is a ≤ 14. Both must hold.
Type it as 13 <= a <= 14.

p1.prompt: A match ball passes inspection only when its inflation pressure P is more than 8.5 psi AND less than 15.6 psi. Type the compound inequality, in the form 8.5 < P < 15.6.
hints: "More than 8.5" is P > 8.5; "less than 15.6" is P < 15.6. Capture both bounds.
Type both bounds as one chain: 8.5 < P < 15.6.

p1.prompt: A player is shown a card if she commits a reckless tackle OR dissents to the referee. Either offense alone earns the card. Using conditions A and B, which describes when she is carded?
hints: Either offense by itself earns the card.
"Either ... or ..." is an OR; both are not required.

p1.prompt: A goalkeeper's distribution is logged as a special play only when it travels less than 6 yards (a short roll-out) OR more than 50 yards (a long launch); normal passes in between are not logged. Let y be the distance in yards. Which describes the logged distributions?
hints: Logged plays are the EXTREMES — very short or very long — not the normal middle range.
A pass can't be both under 6 and over 50 yards, so it must be OR: two separate rays.

p1.prompt: A receiver's route is charted as an intermediate throw only when the air distance y is more than 5 yards AND less than 15 yards downfield. Type the compound inequality, in the form 5 < y < 15.
hints: "More than 5" is y > 5; "less than 15" is y < 15. Both must hold.
Type both bounds as one chain: 5 < y < 15.

p1.prompt: A field-goal attempt is rated "makeable" only when the distance d is at least 20 yards AND at most 50 yards. Type the compound inequality, in the form 20 <= d <= 50.
hints: "At least 20" is d ≥ 20; "at most 50" is d ≤ 50. Capture both bounds.
Type it as 20 <= d <= 50.

p1.prompt: On fourth down, a coach will punt if it is 4th-and-long (8 or more yards to go) OR the ball is behind the team's own 40-yard line. Let g be yards to go and let position be behind own 40. Which describes when the coach punts?
hints: Either situation alone is enough to punt.
"Either ... or ..." is an OR; both conditions need not hold.

p1.prompt: A coaching report flags only the extreme runs: plays that lose yardage (gain less than 0 yards) OR break for explosive gains (more than 20 yards); routine runs in between are not flagged. Let y be the yards gained. Which describes the flagged runs?
hints: Flagged runs are the EXTREMES — losses or explosive gains — not the routine middle.
A play can't both lose yards and gain more than 20, so it must be OR: two separate rays.

p1.prompt: A regulation net height h for co-ed play is set at least 230 cm AND at most 243 cm depending on the division. Type the compound inequality for a legal height, in the form 230 <= h <= 243.
hints: "At least 230" is h ≥ 230; "at most 243" is h ≤ 243. Both must hold.
Type it as 230 <= h <= 243.

p1.prompt: A serve is counted as a controlled jump-float only when its speed s is more than 40 km/h AND less than 60 km/h. Type the compound inequality, in the form 40 < s < 60.
hints: "More than 40" is s > 40; "less than 60" is s < 60. Capture both bounds.
Type both bounds as one chain: 40 < s < 60.

p1.prompt: A set ends when a team reaches 25 or more points OR (in a deciding set) reaches 15 or more points. Let p be a team's points. Which describes when a set can end (ignoring the win-by-two rule)?
hints: A set can end under either scoring rule, depending on which set it is.
"Either ... or ..." is an OR; both thresholds need not be met.

p1.prompt: A stat tool flags only extreme rallies: very short rallies of fewer than 2 contacts (quick aces or errors) OR very long rallies of more than 12 contacts; ordinary rallies in between are not flagged. Let c be the number of contacts. Which describes the flagged rallies?
hints: Flagged rallies are the EXTREMES — very short or very long — not the ordinary middle.
A rally can't have both fewer than 2 and more than 12 contacts, so it must be OR: two separate rays.

p1.prompt: A number x is at least −3 AND at most 4. Type the compound inequality, in the form -3 <= x <= 4.
hints: "At least −3" is x ≥ −3; "at most 4" is x ≤ 4. Both must hold.
Type it as -3 <= x <= 4.

p1.prompt: A number x is greater than 2 AND less than 9. Type the compound inequality, in the form 2 < x < 9.
hints: "Greater than 2" is x > 2; "less than 9" is x < 9. Capture both bounds.
Type both bounds as one chain: 2 < x < 9.

p1.prompt: A number x satisfies x ≤ −1 OR x ≥ 5. Which number line picture matches this solution set?
choices: Two rays: closed dot at −1 shading left, and closed dot at 5 shading right
One segment between −1 and 5 with closed dots at both ends
Two rays: open dot at −1 shading left, and open dot at 5 shading right
One ray: closed dot at −1 shading right

answer.value: Two rays: closed dot at −1 shading left, and closed dot at 5 shading right

hints: OR means a number can be in EITHER piece, so the picture has two separate rays, not one segment.
Both ≤ and ≥ are "or equal to," so both endpoints are CLOSED dots.

p1.prompt: A number x satisfies x < −4 OR x > 1. Which describes the solution set correctly?
choices: Everything to the left of −4 or to the right of 1 (two open rays)

answer.value: Everything to the left of −4 or to the right of 1 (two open rays)

hints: OR keeps the numbers that satisfy EITHER inequality — the outer pieces, not the gap.
The middle between −4 and 1 satisfies neither, so it is excluded; the answer is two outward rays.

p2.prompt: A radar gun records a pitch speed as 2x + 50 mph for a setting x. The pitch falls in the legal drill band when −1 ≤ x ≤ 4. Solve for the speed band by substituting: the speed s satisfies which compound inequality? Type your answer in the form 48 <= s <= 58.
hints: Plug the lower bound x = −1 and the upper bound x = 4 into s = 2x + 50.

p2.prompt: A strike-zone height h (inches) must satisfy 6 ≤ h − 12 ≤ 30 for a particular batter. Solve the compound inequality for h. Type your answer in the form 18 <= h <= 42.
hints: Add 12 to all three parts of the chain at once.

p2.prompt: A pitch count p for a starter must satisfy −10 < 2p − 200 < 10 to stay on the planned target. Solve the compound inequality for p. Type your answer in the form 95 < p < 105.
hints: Add 200 to all three parts, then divide all three parts by 2.
After adding: 190 < 2p < 210. Dividing by the positive 2 keeps the signs: 95 < p < 105.

p2.prompt: A relief-usage rule flags a pitcher when 3x − 1 < −7 OR 3x − 1 > 8, where x is a workload index. Solve each piece. Which is the correct solution set for x?
hints: Solve 3x − 1 < −7 to get x < −2; solve 3x − 1 > 8 to get x > 3.
The two pieces point in opposite directions, so the answer is the UNION x < −2 or x > 3, not the gap between them.

p2.prompt: A pitching-speed reading s (mph) for a legal drill must satisfy 55 ≤ s − 5 ≤ 65 on a gun that reads 5 mph low. Solve the compound inequality for the true speed s. Type your answer in the form 60 <= s <= 70.
hints: Add 5 to all three parts of the chain.

p2.prompt: A legal bat length L (inches) satisfies 52 ≤ 2L ≤ 68 for a sizing chart. Solve the compound inequality for L. Type your answer in the form 26 <= L <= 34.
hints: Divide all three parts by 2.
52 / 2 = 26 and 68 / 2 = 34, so 26 ≤ L ≤ 34. Dividing by positive 2 keeps the directions.

p2.prompt: A travel-team age check requires 13 < a + 1 < 16, where a is the player's age. Solve the compound inequality for a. Type your answer in the form 12 < a < 15.
hints: Subtract 1 from all three parts.

p2.prompt: A machine service alert triggers when 2s − 10 < 70 is FALSE or when 2s − 10 > 130, i.e. service when s < 40 fails... Solve cleanly: service triggers when 2s − 10 < 70 OR 2s − 10 > 130. Which is the correct solution set for s?
hints: Solve 2s − 10 < 70 to get s < 40; solve 2s − 10 > 130 to get s > 70.
The pieces point opposite ways, so the answer is the UNION s < 40 or s > 70, not the middle gap.

p2.prompt: A player's planned minutes m satisfy 24 ≤ m + 4 ≤ 36 in a rotation note. Solve the compound inequality for m. Type your answer in the form 20 <= m <= 32.
hints: Subtract 4 from all three parts.

p2.prompt: A logged scoring run of p unanswered points satisfies 12 < 2p < 28. Solve the compound inequality for p. Type your answer in the form 6 < p < 14.
hints: Divide all three parts by 2.
12 / 2 = 6 and 28 / 2 = 14, so 6 < p < 14. Dividing by positive 2 keeps the directions.

p2.prompt: A shooting-percentage index x satisfies −5 ≤ 3x + 1 ≤ 16. Solve the compound inequality for x. Type your answer in the form -2 <= x <= 5.
hints: Subtract 1 from all three parts, then divide all three by 3.
After subtracting: −6 ≤ 3x ≤ 15. Dividing by positive 3: −2 ≤ x ≤ 5.

p2.prompt: A shot is highlighted on the chart when 2d − 1 < 5 OR 2d − 1 > 47, where d is the distance in feet. Solve each piece. Which is the correct solution set for d?
hints: Solve 2d − 1 < 5 to get d < 3; solve 2d − 1 > 47 to get d > 24.
The pieces go opposite ways, so the answer is the UNION d < 3 or d > 24, not the mid-range gap.

p2.prompt: An eligible age a satisfies 26 ≤ 2a ≤ 28 on a doubled-age roster sheet. Solve the compound inequality for a. Type your answer in the form 13 <= a <= 14.
hints: Divide all three parts by 2.

p2.prompt: A legal match-ball pressure P (psi) satisfies 7.5 < P − 1 < 14.6 on a gauge that reads 1 psi high. Solve the compound inequality for P. Type your answer in the form 8.5 < P < 15.6.
hints: Add 1 to all three parts.

p2.prompt: A passing-accuracy index x satisfies −2 ≤ 4x + 6 ≤ 22. Solve the compound inequality for x. Type your answer in the form -2 <= x <= 4.
hints: Subtract 6 from all three parts, then divide all three by 4.
After subtracting: −8 ≤ 4x ≤ 16. Dividing by positive 4: −2 ≤ x ≤ 4.

p2.prompt: A goalkeeper distribution is logged as special when 2y − 4 < 8 OR 2y − 4 > 96, where y is the distance in yards. Solve each piece. Which is the correct solution set for y?
hints: Solve 2y − 4 < 8 to get y < 6; solve 2y − 4 > 96 to get y > 50.
The pieces point opposite ways, so the answer is the UNION y < 6 or y > 50, not the middle gap.

p2.prompt: An intermediate route's air yardage y satisfies 10 < 2y < 30 on a doubled-distance chart. Solve the compound inequality for y. Type your answer in the form 5 < y < 15.
hints: Divide all three parts by 2.

p2.prompt: A makeable field-goal distance d satisfies 15 ≤ d − 5 ≤ 45 on a worksheet measured from the holder. Solve the compound inequality for d. Type your answer in the form 20 <= d <= 50.
hints: Add 5 to all three parts.

p2.prompt: A passer-efficiency index x satisfies −4 < 5x + 1 < 16. Solve the compound inequality for x. Type your answer in the form -1 < x < 3.
hints: Subtract 1 from all three parts, then divide all three by 5.
After subtracting: −5 < 5x < 15. Dividing by positive 5: −1 < x < 3.

p2.prompt: A run is flagged when 2y + 6 < 6 OR 2y + 6 > 46, where y is the yards gained. Solve each piece. Which is the correct solution set for y?
hints: Solve 2y + 6 < 6 to get y < 0; solve 2y + 6 > 46 to get y > 20.
The pieces point opposite ways, so the answer is the UNION y < 0 or y > 20, not the middle gap.

p2.prompt: A legal net height h (cm) satisfies 225 ≤ h − 5 ≤ 238 on a chart that records the post mark 5 cm above the net. Solve the compound inequality for h. Type your answer in the form 230 <= h <= 243.
hints: Add 5 to all three parts.

p2.prompt: A controlled jump-float serve speed s (km/h) satisfies 80 < 2s < 120 on a doubled readout. Solve the compound inequality for s. Type your answer in the form 40 < s < 60.
hints: Divide all three parts by 2.

p2.prompt: A serve-rating index x satisfies −7 ≤ 3x − 1 ≤ 14. Solve the compound inequality for x. Type your answer in the form -2 <= x <= 5.
hints: Add 1 to all three parts, then divide all three by 3.
After adding: −6 ≤ 3x ≤ 15. Dividing by positive 3: −2 ≤ x ≤ 5.

p2.prompt: A rally is flagged when 2c − 2 < 2 OR 2c − 2 > 22, where c is the number of contacts. Solve each piece. Which is the correct solution set for c?
hints: Solve 2c − 2 < 2 to get c < 2; solve 2c − 2 > 22 to get c > 12.
The pieces point opposite ways, so the answer is the UNION c < 2 or c > 12, not the middle gap.

p2.prompt: Solve the compound inequality -3 ≤ x + 2 < 5. Type your answer as one chain, like -5 <= x < 3.
hints: This is one AND statement: do the same step to all three parts at once.
Subtract 2 from each part: -3 - 2, x, and 5 - 2.

p2.prompt: Solve the compound inequality -7 < 2x - 1 ≤ 9. Type your answer as one chain, like -3 < x <= 5.
hints: Keep all three parts together: add 1 to each, then divide each by 2.
Both endpoints stay finite — an AND statement is bounded on both sides.

p2.prompt: Solve the compound inequality x - 4 < -2 OR x - 4 > 1. Choose the solution set.
hints: Solve each piece separately: add 4 to both sides of each inequality.
OR means union — keep both outer pieces, do not squeeze them into one between-statement.

p2.prompt: Solve the compound inequality 2x + 3 ≤ 1 OR 3x - 2 ≥ 10. Choose the solution set.
hints: Solve each inequality on its own first: 2x + 3 ≤ 1 gives one piece, 3x - 2 ≥ 10 gives the other.
OR keeps both arrows pointing outward — it is not the overlap between -1 and 4.

p3.prompt: Solve the compound inequality and type the solution as a single chain: −2 ≤ x + 1 ≤ 5. Type your answer in the form -3 <= x <= 4.
hints: Subtract 1 from all three parts of the chain at once.

p3.prompt: Solve and type the solution as a single chain: −10 < 2x < 6. Type your answer in the form -5 < x < 3.
hints: Divide all three parts by 2.

p3.prompt: Solve the OR inequality: 2x + 3 < −1 OR 2x + 3 > 11. Which is the correct solution set for x?
hints: Solve 2x + 3 < −1 to get x < −2; solve 2x + 3 > 11 to get x > 4.
The pieces point opposite ways, so the answer is the UNION x < −2 or x > 4, not the gap between them.

p3.prompt: Solve and type the solution as a single chain: 1 ≤ 3x − 2 < 13. Type your answer in the form 1 <= x < 5.
hints: Add 2 to all three parts, then divide all three by 3.
After adding: 3 ≤ 3x < 15. Dividing by positive 3: 1 ≤ x < 5 — note the left end is closed and the right end is open.

p3.prompt: A solution set is described as x ≤ −1 OR x ≥ 3. Which number line graph is correct?
choices: Closed dot at −1 shading left, and closed dot at 3 shading right (two rays)
Closed dots at −1 and 3 with the segment between them shaded
Open dot at −1 shading left, and open dot at 3 shading right (two rays)
A single shaded ray from −1 to the right through 3

answer.value: Closed dot at −1 shading left, and closed dot at 3 shading right (two rays)

hints: OR keeps the OUTER pieces (two rays), not the inner segment between the bounds.
Both ≤ and ≥ include the endpoint, so both dots are CLOSED.

p3.prompt: Solve the OR inequality: 4x − 5 ≤ −13 OR 2x + 1 > 9. Which is the correct solution set for x?
hints: Solve 4x − 5 ≤ −13 to get x ≤ −2; solve 2x + 1 > 9 to get x > 4.
The pieces point opposite ways, so the answer is the UNION x ≤ −2 or x > 4 — keep the closed end on −2 and the open end on 4.
